Home.aboutLead: ViraStack is an open-source ecosystem that brings long-term quality and architectural order to frontend projects.
Home.aboutBody1: AI makes writing code faster, but without the right foundation, technical debt, performance losses, and accessibility gaps pile up.
Home.aboutBody2: With a predefined architecture and best practices, ViraStack puts your project on solid ground from day one and helps keep rewrite and maintenance costs low.
Home.aboutBody3: You need to know the right foundation before you can build on it. ViraStack also offers a free, carefully sourced roadmap for anyone who wants to learn frontend in order, from the fundamentals to advanced topics.

Ai.demoVideoLabel: ViraStack AI demo: one command installs the rules, and each check shows the agent’s code before and after the rules.
Ai.rulesDesc: One command writes Claude Code and Cursor rules to their own folders (.claude/rules and .cursor/rules), plus a rule map in AGENTS.md for every other agent. Only the rules that fit your project are installed from a catalog of 14.
Ai.rulesArchDesc: Folder structure and feature boundaries stay fixed, so the agent puts every file in the right place, even as the project grows.
Ai.rulesDataDesc: Server data lives in TanStack Query, client state in Zustand and nuqs, and failures go through one ApiError.
Ai.rulesUiDesc: The agent builds forms with <rhf>React Hook Form</rhf> and <zod>Zod</zod>, and the UI with <shadcn>shadcn/ui</shadcn> and <tailwind>Tailwind CSS</tailwind> 4. The i18n rule is added only with next-intl or Paraglide.
Ai.rulesQualityDesc: The code an agent writes follows <react>React</react> 19 patterns and strict <typescript>TypeScript</typescript>, and its tests use <vitest>Vitest</vitest>, <testinglibrary>Testing Library</testinglibrary> and MSW.
Ai.rulesPerfDesc: LCP, INP and CLS budgets are set; the agent starts every optimization by measuring first instead of guessing.
Ai.rulesFwDesc: Only your framework’s rules are written, so the agent never mixes in another framework’s APIs.
Ai.howDesc: Three steps: it learns your project, writes the rules and shares them with other agents. With <start>Start</start>, these steps run automatically for a new project.
Ai.how1Body: It reads package.json and the lockfile, so it knows whether you use Next.js or TanStack Start, which i18n library you have and your package manager.
Ai.how2Body: Rules go to .claude/rules/virastack and .cursor/rules/virastack. Each rule applies when the agent touches matching files, and the core rules are always loaded.
Ai.how3Title: One shared map for other agents
Ai.how3Body: A block in AGENTS.md lists every rule. Codex, Copilot and other agents that read AGENTS.md follow the same architecture.

Ai.ctaDesc: <start>Start</start> scaffolds a production-ready <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> or <tanstack>TanStack Start</tanstack> project in one command. Feature-based architecture, type safety and these AI rules are included.

Start.demoVideoLabel: ViraStack Start setup: answer the prompts and get a project with AI rules ready.
Start.featuresCliDesc: Answer a few questions and the project, dependencies, AI rules and first commit are ready. Add tools later with one command, or run it <bold>without prompts in CI</bold>.
Start.featuresStackDesc: Pick <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> or <tanstack>TanStack Start</tanstack>; the folder structure, rules and tooling stay the same. React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, Base UI and Motion come ready.
Start.featuresFsdDesc: Each feature keeps its api, components, hooks, schemas and stores together. As the project grows, it stays clear where code belongs.
Start.featuresTypesDesc: Strict <typescript>TypeScript</typescript> and <zod>Zod</zod> keep data flow type-safe from the start. Vitest, Testing Library and MSW come set up for tests.
Start.featuresStateDesc: Server data, UI state and URL state each get their own tool. It stays clear where each piece of data lives, so <bold>the code stays untangled</bold>.
Start.featuresAiDesc: <claudecode>Claude Code</claudecode> and <cursor>Cursor</cursor> rules, plus three design skills, come with setup. Agents write code that fits your architecture from day one.

Mask.featuresRhfDesc: Your form keeps the <bold>clean value</bold> while users see it neatly formatted. Your existing <rhf>React Hook Form</rhf> code keeps working as it is.
Mask.featuresPresetsDesc: TCKN, VKN, IBAN, phone numbers and lira amounts work with Turkish rules out of the box. The bank’s name is detected as the IBAN is typed.
Mask.featuresValidationDesc: Define a mask once and use the same one in a Server Action. The server receives the clean, unformatted value.
Mask.featuresCustomDesc: Describe your own formats, like a plate or reference code, in a few lines. Write it once and reuse it everywhere.
Mask.featuresLightDesc: The whole package is under <bold>10 KB</bold> (min+brotli) with no dependencies. Only the parts you use end up in your project.
Mask.featuresRulesDesc: Card numbers are checked with the <bold>Luhn</bold> algorithm and IBANs with the <bold>mod-97</bold> algorithm. Past expiry dates and age limits are covered too.

Password.featuresA11yDesc: Screen reader labels, focus that returns to the input and the Caps Lock state come ready. The password hides on submit and works with password managers.
Password.featuresHeadlessDesc: Only props, so the look is entirely yours. The hook is about 2 KB min+brotli with no dependencies; the strength check only joins your bundle when you use it.
Password.featuresStrengthDesc: Looks at <bold>length</bold> instead of forcing capitals and symbols, and catches common passwords, repeats and personal info.
Password.featuresServerDesc: The same password rules run in the form and in the Server Action; you don’t rewrite them on the server, so the two never drift apart.
Password.featuresPwnedDesc: Checked against known breaches through Have I Been Pwned. Only <bold>the first 5 characters of the password’s hash</bold> are sent, and a failed check never blocks the user.
Password.featuresI18nDesc: Errors come back as <bold>keys</bold> rather than ready-made messages. You show the text in any language with your own translation setup.

AboutPage.title: About
AboutPage.description: The story behind ViraStack: from Turkuaz to an open-source ecosystem for frontend developers.
AboutPage.intro:
ViraStack is an open-source ecosystem that brings long-term quality and architectural order to frontend projects. It offers free guides, production-ready starters, AI rules, and headless form hooks. The goal is simple: instead of rebuilding the foundation every time, build your product.

It is made for developers working with React, Next.js, and TanStack Start.
AboutPage.whatBody1: The ecosystem’s products do three jobs. To set up a project, <start>Start</start>: feature-based, production-ready templates with <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> and <tanstackstart>TanStack Start</tanstackstart>. To keep AI agents writing code that fits your project, <ai>AI</ai>: architecture rules. For forms, headless hooks: <mask>Mask</mask> for input masks, <password>Password</password> for password fields and <address>Address</address> for address forms.
AboutPage.whatBody2: With <academy>Academy</academy>, you can learn frontend step by step, from the basics to advanced topics. Every source is an official doc, a recognized engineer, or an independent institution; <sources>see the criteria</sources>. To see how a modern web app is built in 3 minutes, there is <guide>Guide</guide>.
AboutPage.learnBody: I’ve always learned frontend by building in public. Years ago, when Bootstrap defined the era, I shipped <turkuaz>Turkuaz</turkuaz>; a CSS framework I wrote to understand CSS deeply. That instinct hasn’t changed. I still build to stay current; only how I build has.
AboutPage.formBody: The real time sink is usually the project skeleton, the conventions, the hooks you rewrite every time, and the rules that keep an AI agent from writing code at random. <virastack>ViraStack</virastack> sits right there: feature-based structure, starters, hooks, and agent rules; a ready foundation you can pick up and run with.
AboutPage.principlesIntro: Every new package and every change goes through the same four principles.
AboutPage.principle1Body: <react>React</react>, <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs>, <tanstackbadge>TanStack</tanstackbadge>, and <rhf>React Hook Form</rhf> are already good. ViraStack doesn’t compete with them; it builds on top of them and makes the pieces every project rewrites, once and with care.
AboutPage.principle2Body: The form packages bring no markup or styles; they work with your own components. Types ship with each package; <mask>Mask</mask> checks field names against your form’s type. It works together with <password>Password</password> and <address>Address</address> in one form.
AboutPage.principle3Title: Ready for Turkey, open to the world
AboutPage.principle3Body: TCKN, VKN, IBAN, and address data come built in; global needs like phone, card, date, and currency are supported from day one.
AboutPage.principle4Body: Every fact in a comparison table is checked against its source, package sizes are measured in the same scenario, and promises are backed by tests. We avoid writing anything we can’t verify.
AboutPage.nameBody1: Before ViraStack, the organization was briefly called Vassale; a nod to a craft of joining pieces, and to bringing projects together. It was hard to discover, awkward for SEO, and too close to the English word <italic>vassal</italic>. So I looked for something else: workable as a global brand, still carrying a small thread of Turkish culture.
AboutPage.nameBody2: That word was <bold>Vira!</bold>; a call fishermen on Turkey’s Black Sea coast use when hauling nets or lines, roughly “heave!” or “haul!” I paired it with Stack, and you get ViraStack: <start>Start</start>, <ai>AI</ai>, <mask>Mask</mask>, and the rest.
AboutPage.nameBody3: The turquoise in our logo is deliberate too: it comes from Turkuaz CSS, and I still love that color.
AboutPage.refsBody: When I look at <shadcn>shadcn</shadcn>, I see the path I was chasing with Turkuaz; they carried it much further. <tanner>Tanner</tanner> is a master of this craft. <tanstack>TanStack</tanstack> is both a clear bar for sustainable open source and an inspiration for the name: Vira + Stack. I’m grateful to both.
AboutPage.closeBody: Yesterday there was Turkuaz. Today there’s ViraStack. In tomorrow’s frontend world, I’ll be building something again.

BrandPage.title: Brand
BrandPage.description: ViraStack logo, naming, typography, and product colors, icons, and descriptions.
BrandPage.intro: Logo, naming, typography, color, icon, and product description rules for the ViraStack brand. The same language is used across product pages and in copy.
BrandPage.logoBody: Use the mark alone or with the wordmark. The wordmark is always written as ViraStack; never apply CSS uppercase.
BrandPage.lockupBody: In large areas (heroes) a black product name overlaps the outlined ViraStack wordmark. In small areas (header, footer, running text) the same name sits bold next to the wordmark. In both cases the product name is never italic and always in its own color. The outline is neutral decoration only.
BrandPage.dotsBody: Seven dots, one per product, always in this order: Academy, Start, AI, Mask, Password, Address, Guide. Hover or focus a dot to see just the product name, as the brand already sits above the dots; each one links to its product. On the home page they appear once the intro animation ends.
BrandPage.namingBody: In text, always write the full lockup: <mask>Mask</mask>. Where the brand already sits right beside or above, such as the product dots and the footer product list, the product name alone is used. There the full name stays in the accessible label.
BrandPage.typeBody: Two tiers. Display (heroes): ViraStack and the product name are both black. UI (header, footer, running text): ViraStack is semibold and the product name bold.
BrandPage.colorsBody: Each product maps to a <tailwind>Tailwind CSS</tailwind> color and one icon from <lucide>Lucide</lucide>. The swatch is the fixed brand shade (dots, glows, OG images, badges); text and icons use one shade darker on light backgrounds so they stay readable. The icon is shown in the product color in navigation, search and cards; never as inline decoration in running text.
BrandPage.copyBody: Every product is described in three lengths, all from one config file: the short text in the header menu and search, the medium text on the home page ecosystem cards, the long text in the product page hero. A short meta description is written separately for search results (about 155 characters); without one, the long text is used.

Academy.contributeWhyP1: Working with AI agents sped up the work, but it also reduced how much we write and read code. Foundations and architecture decisions fade from memory over time, and there is so much to read that even choosing which sources to trust takes time.
Academy.contributeWhyP2: Academy offers curated learning for everyone from junior to senior, drawn from official docs, recognized engineers, and independent institutions. It is free and has no ads.

Personal blogs and content with unclear identity fall outside these criteria. <sources>Review the criteria</sources>.
Academy.contributeFaqPaidQ: Are paid courses or affiliate content accepted?

Academy.contributeFaqErrorQ: I found an error in a guide. What should I do?
Academy.contributeFaqErrorA: <githubIssue>Open an issue on GitHub</githubIssue>. Naming the guide and the incorrect part is enough.
Academy.contributeFaqTopicQ: Can I suggest a new guide topic?
Academy.contributeFaqTopicA: Yes. Share the topic and the level by <githubIssue>opening an issue on GitHub</githubIssue>, and we’ll review it.
Academy.contributeFaqUpdateA: Each guide shows a last-verified date at the bottom. When tools ship new versions, related guides are checked again.

Academy.sourcesCriteriaEngineerBody: A maintainer of the tool, a member of the core team, or an engineer who speaks regularly at major conferences. What they write rests on experience gained in production.
Academy.sourcesCriteriaInstitutionBody: A university, standards body, or engineering publication from a large technology company that is not tied to a commercial tool. It rests on measured data and experience at large scale.

Guide.learnContentDesc: Every interface starts with content, and style comes after. The guide opens with plain text and builds on it step by step.
Guide.learnStackDesc: A modern interface isn’t built with HTML and CSS alone. Its architecture comes from <react>React</react> and <typescript>TypeScript</typescript> with <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> or <tanstack>TanStack Start</tanstack> on top.
Guide.learnStyleDesc: A readable page starts with layout. <tailwind>Tailwind CSS</tailwind> sets spacing and alignment in seconds, with no hand-written CSS.
Guide.learnTypeDesc: The default font makes a page look unfinished. Pick a font in the guide and every later step changes with it.
Guide.learnUiDesc: Compose with <shadcn>shadcn/ui</shadcn> instead of reinventing controls. Watch a mask format the card number, expiry date and CVV, live.
Guide.learnAiDesc: Add light and dark themes, then type a request and watch AI build a full interface from scratch.
Guide.step0Body: Every interface starts with content. Design’s job is to make that text readable. The web’s foundation is semantic content; we build style on top of it.
Guide.step1Body: The traditional web was HTML and CSS. Today’s standard is a modern frontend architecture built with <react>React</react>, <typescript>TypeScript</typescript>, <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs>, and <tanstack>TanStack Start</tanstack>.
Guide.step2Body: Readability starts with the right layout. Instead of writing CSS by hand, we handle alignment and spacing in seconds with <tailwind>Tailwind CSS</tailwind>.
Guide.step3Body: The browser’s default fonts make a product feel unfinished. Typography sets the tone of the interface; choosing a font changes the visual language of every step.
Guide.step4Body: Building accessible components from scratch takes time. With <shadcn>shadcn/ui</shadcn> we compose flexible components, and <mask>Mask</mask> tidies up the card number, expiry date and CVV.
Guide.step5Body: Dark mode is now a standard expectation. We add theme switches that respect system or user preference in just a few lines.
Guide.step6Body: Development workflows are evolving. Instead of writing code line by line, we ship AI-assisted, dynamic interfaces with the right prompts.
Guide.step6Prompt: Make a map showing Istanbul; include zoom and location buttons.
Guide.step7Body: We completed the journey from plain HTML to an AI-assisted interface.

DocsAi.introductionDescription: ViraStack AI installs one set of architecture rules for Claude Code, Cursor and every AGENTS.md agent.
DocsAi.introductionHeaderDesc: What ViraStack AI does, why it exists and the one command that installs it.
DocsAi.introductionLead: ViraStack AI (@virastack/ai) writes architecture rules for AI coding agents into a Next.js or TanStack Start project. The rules describe where code lives, which libraries to use and how, so agents write code that matches the rest of the project.
DocsAi.introductionWhatNative: Writes 14 rules in each tool’s native format: .claude/rules/virastack/ for Claude Code and .cursor/rules/virastack/ for Cursor.
DocsAi.introductionWhatMap: Adds a managed block to AGENTS.md with the project’s commands and a map of every rule, so Codex, Copilot and other agents find them too.
DocsAi.introductionWhatFramework: Detects Next.js or TanStack Start from package.json and installs only that framework’s rules. The i18n rule is added only when next-intl or Paraglide is installed.
DocsAi.introductionWhatManifest: Records every installed file in .virastack/ai.json, so updates replace only rules you did not change.
DocsAi.introductionWhySame: <bold>One standard, every tool:</bold> a team using <claudecode>Claude Code</claudecode> and <cursor>Cursor</cursor> side by side gets the same rules in both.
DocsAi.introductionWhyStack: <bold>Written for the current stack:</bold> <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> 16, <react>React</react> 19.2, <tanstackstart>TanStack Start</tanstackstart>, <tanstackquery>TanStack Query</tanstackquery> 5, <zustand>Zustand</zustand> 5, <zod>Zod</zod> 4 and <tailwind>Tailwind CSS</tailwind> 4. Every example follows its own rules.
DocsAi.introductionWhySafe: Never overwrites your files: rules live in their own virastack/ folders. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md only get a small managed block or import line.
DocsAi.introductionQuickP: Run it in the project root:
DocsAi.introductionQuickStart: Starting a new project? <start>ViraStack Start</start> scaffolds <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> or <tanstackstart>TanStack Start</tanstackstart> with these rules already installed.

DocsAi.rulesCatalogPerformance: LCP, INP and CLS budgets, measure before optimizing, images, fonts and scripts.
DocsAi.rulesCatalogTesting: <vitest>Vitest</vitest>, Testing Library and MSW: behavior over implementation, role queries, HTTP mocked with MSW.

DocsAi.rulesCatalogTanstackStart: File routes, loaders with ensureQueryData, server functions with createServerFn, middleware, head().

DocsStart.introductionDescription: Create a production-ready Next.js or TanStack Start project with a single ViraStack Start command.
DocsStart.introductionDesc: <start></start> is a production-focused CLI that creates a modern React project in one command.
DocsStart.introductionP1: It cuts configuration fatigue with <nextjs>Next.js</nextjs> or <tanstack>TanStack Start</tanstack> templates, feature-based architecture, strict <typescript>TypeScript</typescript>, and AI agent rules.
DocsStart.introductionP2: Optional ecosystem tools such as <mask>Mask</mask>, <password>Password</password> and <address>Address</address> can be selected during setup.
DocsStart.introductionGettingStartedP: Ready to create a project? Follow <installation>installation</installation>. For flags and non-interactive use see <cli>CLI</cli>; for framework and folder layout see <templates>templates</templates>.
DocsStart.introductionWhyCli: <bold>Interactive CLI</bold>: guided setup instead of a long flag checklist.
DocsStart.introductionWhyProd: <bold>Production-ready base</bold>: ESLint, Prettier, Husky, Knip, Commitlint, and CI come ready.
DocsStart.introductionWhyAgent: <bold>Agent-ready</bold>: setup writes <ai>AI</ai> rules for the AI coding tools you pick and installs three design skills, so assistants match the project architecture.
DocsStart.introductionWhatsInP: Every template ships a feature-based layout, theme support, Zod env validation, and the same shared packages for state, forms, and UI. The full list with icons is on the <templates>templates → shared stack</templates> page. Optional multi-language setup is covered under <i18n>i18n</i18n>.
DocsStart.introductionOutOfScope: Auth and database are intentionally out of scope; the architecture is left ready for you to add them when needed. Tests come ready with Vitest, Testing Library and MSW.

DocsPassword.introductionDescription: Headless password hook for React: show/hide, NIST-style strength, confirmation, server validation and leaked password checks.
DocsPassword.useViraPasswordDescription: Hook API: every option, the return value and how props merge.
DocsPassword.accessibilityDescription: ARIA, focus after a click, a live region for strength and Caps Lock.
DocsPassword.customizationDescription: Icons, text, props, automatic hiding, autoComplete and locked states.
DocsPassword.helpersDescription: mergeProps, composeRefs, core helpers and the default icons.
DocsPassword.uiLibrariesDescription: Password is not tied to a UI. Same pattern with shadcn, Ant Design, Chakra, or plain inputs.
DocsPassword.examplesDescription: Live previews. Click one for details and code.
DocsPassword.exampleBasicDescription: Simplest show/hide usage with default icons and ARIA.
DocsPassword.exampleBasicNote1: Default visibility is false; starts with input type=password.
DocsPassword.exampleBasicNote2: Eye icons come from the package; no extra setup needed.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomIconsDescription: Use your own SVG or components via icons.show / icons.hide.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomIconsNote0: show: when password is hidden (show button).
DocsPassword.exampleCustomIconsNote1: hide: when password is visible (hide button).
DocsPassword.exampleCustomIconsNote2: icons accepts ReactNode: icon, text, or any JSX.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomTextDescription: Use text like “Show” / “Hide” instead of icons. icons still accepts ReactNode.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomTextNote0: There is no separate text API; icons.show / icons.hide accept string or JSX.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomTextNote1: show: label when password is hidden.
DocsPassword.exampleCustomTextNote2: hide: label when password is visible.
DocsPassword.exampleDisabledDescription: When disabled or readOnly, the toggle is locked and visibility cannot change.
DocsPassword.exampleDisabledNote0: disabled: true → input and button disabled.
DocsPassword.exampleDisabledNote1: readOnly: true → input readOnly, button disabled.
DocsPassword.examplePropMergeDescription: Merge name, autoComplete, className, and handlers with inputProps and btnProps.
DocsPassword.examplePropMergeNote0: User props merge with base props.
DocsPassword.examplePropMergeNote1: on* handlers are chained; className is merged.
DocsPassword.examplePropMergeNote2: This example is not a form library; it shows prop merge behavior.
DocsPassword.exampleProgrammaticDescription: Control visibility from code with isVisible, toggle, and setVisible.
DocsPassword.exampleProgrammaticNote0: The hook return includes isVisible, toggle(), and setVisible(visible).
DocsPassword.exampleProgrammaticNote2: hideOnBlur hides the password again when focus leaves the field; submitting the form hides it by default.
DocsPassword.exampleProgrammaticNote3: When disabled / readOnly, the programmatic API is also a no-op.
DocsPassword.upgradeDescription: 1.1 adds features without breaking the hook. A few defaults changed; each can be turned off.
DocsPassword.strengthDescription: NIST-style password policy with @virastack/password/strength: length, common passwords, repeats and personal info.
DocsPassword.confirmDescription: Repeat-password fields with the same hook and matchWith.
DocsPassword.rhfDescription: Use the hook with register, Controller, Zod and ViraStack Mask in one form.
DocsPassword.serverDescription: Run the same policy in Server Actions and API routes with @virastack/password/server.
DocsPassword.pwnedDescription: Optional Have I Been Pwned check with k-anonymity: @virastack/password/pwned.
DocsPassword.exampleShowHideDescription: Toggle with focus handling, hiding on submit and a Caps Lock hint.
DocsPassword.exampleShowHideNote0: A mouse click returns focus to the input; Enter or Space keeps it on the button.
DocsPassword.exampleShowHideNote1: The password is hidden again when the form is submitted.
DocsPassword.exampleShowHideNote2: capsLock is true while Caps Lock is on and the input has focus.
DocsPassword.exampleStrengthDescription: Your own bar on top of score, level and issue keys.
DocsPassword.exampleStrengthNote0: The policy comes from definePolicy(); the hook only evaluates it.
DocsPassword.exampleStrengthNote1: strengthProps makes the text a polite live region.
DocsPassword.exampleStrengthNote2: Issues are keys; the messages map is yours.
DocsPassword.exampleConfirmDescription: A repeat field with matchWith; matches is true, false or null.
DocsPassword.exampleConfirmNote0: matches is null while the confirm field is empty.
DocsPassword.exampleConfirmNote1: Each field has its own show/hide button.
DocsPassword.exampleRhfZodDescription: The same policy inside a Zod schema, with register and useWatch.
DocsPassword.exampleRhfZodNote0: mergeProps keeps both the hook's and register()'s handlers.
DocsPassword.exampleRhfZodNote1: value comes from useWatch, so reset() and setValue() are followed.
DocsPassword.exampleRhfZodNote2: Zod returns the keys; the message map turns them into text.
DocsPassword.exampleServerDescription: A plain form posting to a Server Action that checks the same policy.
DocsPassword.exampleServerNote1: forbidden and confirm are checked on the server too.
DocsPassword.exampleForbiddenDescription: Reject passwords that contain the user's email or name.
DocsPassword.exampleForbiddenNote0: Emails are split into the local part and its pieces; the domain is ignored.
DocsPassword.exampleForbiddenNote1: Pieces shorter than minTokenLength (default 3) are ignored.
DocsPassword.exampleForbiddenNote2: Case, accents and simple leetspeak are ignored.
DocsPassword.examplePwnedDescription: Check Have I Been Pwned from a Server Action.
DocsPassword.examplePwnedNote0: Only the first 5 characters of the SHA-1 hash leave the server.
DocsPassword.examplePwnedNote1: Calling it from the server keeps the user's IP away from HIBP.
DocsPassword.examplePwnedNote2: On any failure the status is unknown; never block the user.
DocsPassword.exampleMaskSignupDescription: Phone (ViraStack Mask), password and confirm in one React Hook Form.
DocsPassword.exampleMaskSignupNote0: Mask and Password share one useForm but never the same input.
DocsPassword.exampleMaskSignupNote1: deps re-checks the confirm field when the password changes.
DocsPassword.exampleMaskSignupNote2: The form holds the raw phone value and the password.

DocsPasswordV1.customizationDescription: Custom icons, text, input/button props, and style merging.

DocsAddress.introductionDescription: A headless React hook for Turkish addresses: province, district and neighbourhood picked in a chain, the postal code derived from the pick, server validation and the PTT dataset.
DocsAddress.useViraAddressDescription: The hook API: options, the return value, the value object and bringing your own data.
DocsAddress.reactHookFormDescription: Pass a form and every pick is written into it: default field names, names, FormProvider, edit forms and Zod.
DocsAddress.postalCodeDescription: Type a postal code and the selects fill in: all three levels for a code with one neighbourhood, province and district for a shared one.
DocsAddress.uiLibrariesDescription: Prop getters fill a plain select in one line and work out the disabled state from the chain, with flavours for shadcn/ui, Ant Design and your own component.
DocsAddress.serverDescription: Re-check a submitted address against the dataset with @virastack/address/server, and derive the postal code on the server.
DocsAddress.dataDescription: 81 provinces, 973 districts and 72,466 neighbourhoods with postal codes. No React needed; each province loads only when it is needed.
DocsAddress.helpersDescription: formatName, toSearchKey, compareNames and formatAddress: display, search and sort Turkish names and put an address on one line, with İ and ı handled correctly.

DocsMask.introductionDescription: Zero-dependency input masks for React Hook Form, with Turkish validators, type safety and server support.
DocsMask.upgradeDescription: v2 is a rewrite. The hook signature, the preset list and some values changed.
DocsMask.upgradeHeadingPrompt: One step with an AI agent
DocsMask.useViraMaskDescription: Mask several fields with one hook. The form keeps the raw value; the input shows the mask.
DocsMask.customMaskDescription: Pattern syntax, custom tokens, optional and fixed parts, dynamic masks, number and date options.
DocsMask.validationDescription: Errors come back as keys, not messages. Add your own rules and use them with a resolver.
DocsMask.serverDescription: Use the same schema in Server Components and Server Actions with @virastack/mask/server.
DocsMask.helpersDescription: Pure mask, validator and money functions you can use outside the hook.
DocsMask.banksDescription: Find the bank behind a Turkish IBAN. No API: the bank is read from the bank code inside the number.
DocsMask.uiLibrariesDescription: Mask is not a UI package. The same pattern works with shadcn/ui, Ant Design, Chakra and plain inputs.
DocsMask.examplesDescription: Live previews of every preset. Click one for details and customization.
DocsMask.examplesPageHeaderDescription: Live previews of every preset. Click a title for code and customization.
DocsMask.exampleCreditCardDescription: Card number, expiry and CVV together. Entering an Amex switches the CVV to 4 digits.
DocsMask.exampleCreditCardNote0: The CVV links to the card with from: "card". The link is explicit; the schema is not scanned.
DocsMask.exampleCreditCardNote1: An Amex card (34, 37) is grouped 4-6-5 and its CVV has 4 digits. If the card turns into a Visa, the CVV is trimmed to 3 digits on screen and in the form.
DocsMask.exampleCreditCardNote2: The card is checked with Luhn; the expiry rejects past months.
DocsMask.exampleCardDescription: Credit and debit card numbers. Visa, Mastercard, Amex and Troy are detected; Amex switches the pattern.
DocsMask.exampleCardNote0: Validation: length for the network and Luhn.
DocsMask.exampleCardNote1: The form value is digits only.
DocsMask.exampleCardCustomization0Description: Read the network from the form value with getCardType.
DocsMask.exampleCardCustomization1Description: onComplete runs when the mask is full. You decide where focus goes.
DocsMask.exampleExpiryDescription: MM/YY. Corrected while typing (2 → 02/); past months are invalid.
DocsMask.exampleExpiryNote0: The month can't pass 12; typing 13 drops the 3.
DocsMask.exampleCvvDescription: 3-digit security code; 4 digits when the linked card is an Amex.
DocsMask.exampleCvvNote0: Without a linked card it has 3 digits.
DocsMask.exampleCvvNote1: See the credit card form example for the full setup.
DocsMask.exampleCvvCustomization0Description: from must be a real field name; a wrong name is a type error.
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyDescription: Separators and symbol from Intl. Default 1,234.56 without a symbol; with a code $1,234.56. For Turkish lira use country: "TR". The form value is 1234.56.
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyNote0: Kuruş is kept. Both a dot and a comma can be typed as the decimal.
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyNote1: For math, toMinorUnits returns an integer without float errors.
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyCustomization0Description: Link it to a select with from; the format follows the currency and the form value stays the same.
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyCustomization1Description: An ISO code, a BCP 47 locale, min and max.
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyCustomization2Description: Payment providers (Stripe, Adyen, iyzico) expect the amount as an integer in the smallest unit: 1,234.56 TRY = 123456 kuruş. Doing math with floats gives errors like 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004; toMinorUnits converts the text to an integer exactly.
DocsMask.exampleVknDescription: 10-digit Turkish tax number, checked with the VKN algorithm.
DocsMask.exampleIbanDescription: IBAN for every country: groups of 4, uppercase, length for the country and mod-97 validation.
DocsMask.exampleIbanNote0: The country code sets the length (TR 26, DE 22…); countries outside the registry use the 15–34 rule.
DocsMask.examplePhoneDescription: International (E.164) numbers: + and up to 15 digits; typing +90 switches to the Turkish layout. For Turkish input use country: "TR".
DocsMask.examplePhoneNote0: There is no per-country format table; other countries are shown without grouping. A leading 00 is dropped.
DocsMask.exampleNumberDescription: Integers with thousands separators (1,234). Add decimals, a sign, min and max; country: "TR" for Turkish separators.
DocsMask.exampleNumberNote0: Max applies while typing, min on blur.
DocsMask.exampleNumberCustomization0Description: min, max, scale (fraction digits), signed and locale.
DocsMask.exampleDateDescription: DD/MM/YYYY. Corrected while typing; the form value is ISO (2026-07-29).
DocsMask.exampleDateNote0: Typing 4 gives 04/; the month can't pass 12, the day 31; 31/02 is invalid.
DocsMask.exampleDateNote1: reset and setValue accept ISO: setValue("date", "2026-07-29").
DocsMask.exampleDateCustomization0Description: Dates after today and under 18 are invalid.
DocsMask.exampleDateCustomization1Description: The end date links to the start with from and can't be before it.
DocsMask.exampleDateCustomization2Description: DD/MM/YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD, DD.MM.YYYY, MM/YY, MM/YYYY.
DocsMask.exampleCustomDescription: Write your own pattern: 9 digit, a letter, [ ] optional part.
DocsMask.exampleCustomNote1: The error key comes from the preset name: plate.incomplete.
DocsMask.exampleCustomCustomization0Description: Define it once; the hook, the server and tests use the same mask.
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyCustomization2Code:
import { toMinorUnits } from "@virastack/mask"

const price = form.getValues("price") // "1234.56"
toMinorUnits(price, "TRY")           // 123456 (kuruş)
toMinorUnits("19.99", "USD")         // 1999 (cents)
toMinorUnits("1500", "JPY")          // 1500 (yen has no minor unit)
DocsMask.exampleNumberCustomization1Description: country: "TR" uses a dot for thousands and a comma for decimals.
DocsMask.examplePasswordDescription: ViraStack Mask and ViraStack Password together: the password is registered as is, the 6-digit PIN is masked, and both have show/hide.
DocsMask.examplePasswordNote0: Passwords are not masked, which is why v1's password preset was removed. Show/hide is Password's job.
DocsMask.examplePasswordNote1: The packages fit together: Password's inputProps holds attributes only (type, id, autoComplete, disabled, readOnly, aria), with no ref or handlers, so it spreads onto a masked input without conflicts: '{'...pin'}' '{'...inputProps'}'.
DocsMask.exampleCreditCardCheckDescription: The card number is checked for its network's length and the Luhn checksum, the expiry for invalid and past months. The CVV switches between 3 and 4 digits with the card type.
DocsMask.exampleCardCheckDescription: Length for the network (Amex 15, others 16) and the Luhn checksum. Every single-digit error and most swapped neighbours are caught; the error is card.invalid.
DocsMask.exampleTcknCheckDescription: 11 digits, not starting with 0; the 10th and 11th digits follow the official algorithm. Every single-digit typo is caught; the error is tckn.invalid.
DocsMask.exampleVknCheckDescription: The last digit is checked with the Turkish Revenue Administration's tax number algorithm; the error is vkn.invalid.
DocsMask.exampleIbanCheckDescription: The country code sets the length (TR 26, DE 22, GB 22…), then the ISO 13616 mod-97 checksum runs. Lengths for more than 90 countries are built in.
DocsMask.exampleExpiryCheckDescription: Month 13 can't be typed and 2 becomes 02/ while typing. A past month returns expiry.min.
DocsMask.exampleDateCheckDescription: While typing the month can't pass 12 and the day 31; 4 becomes 04/. Dates that don't exist such as 31/02 are rejected. min/max (including today), minimum age (minAge) and start–end (from) are built in.
DocsMask.cardNetworksIntro: The network comes from the leading digits; the pattern, length and CVV digits follow it.
DocsMask.exampleCurrencyTRCustomizationDescriptio: country: "TR" uses the TRY symbol and Turkish separators: ₺1.234,56. The form value is still 1234.56.
DocsMask.examplePhoneCustomization0Description: country: "TR" gives (555) 123 45 67. Users can start with +90, 0 or the number itself; all give the same result. The form value has 10 digits.
DocsMask.examplePhoneCustomization1Description: Some backends want the masked text; output: "masked" writes the display text into the form.
DocsMask.exampleIbanCustomization0Description: With country: "TR" the TR prefix is written for you and kept in the value, and a digit keyboard opens. A pasted TR33 0006… is read correctly too.
